scope: Five-family staged SPI DMA coexistence, preserved PIO and existing DMA backends, ordinary example adaptations, and the complete actual main ARM matrix.

source_review.conclusion: No unresolved runtime, build-qualification or example-source finding.
coverage: Independent PIO qualification plus explicit new DMA controller counts and exact RX/TX selectors
Borrowed PIO constructors and static-only DMA constructor resources, sequential admission and consumed-on-error behavior
Single lifetime-generic async method/trait surface, fixed owner-local dispatch, and settlement before every empty operation
One dedicated handler with separately active-guarded PIO/DMA dispatch and unchanged native L012 SPI23 handling
Unchanged bounded PIO poll, wake, preparation, cancellation, sticky configuration-error and destructive recovery rules
Paired private staging, RX-first arm/request order, complete dual terminal proof, error-free wire idle and fenced retirement before CPU RX visibility
Common PIO-before-DMA blocking guards and bounded Drop with unresolved DMA resources retained
Exact feature, native channel/vector, AF5 pin, PB0 CS, family speed, workload and metadata-linker adaptations

closed_finding.description: New DMA cfg initially suppressed automatic Send/Sync for existing PIO and blocking owners through a private raw pointer.
closed_finding.resolution: Independently reviewed private non-Copy OwnedRxStaging consumes exclusive static byte storage, alone carries justified Send/Sync, and keeps outer fields compiler checked. Private RX copy and both callers now require mutable pair access after successful retirement.
closed_finding.compatibility: Restores prior PIO/blocking availability on new DMA families and positively permits existing F030/A030/L083 DMA/blocking owners to satisfy these traits, subject to other fields and borrow lifetimes. It does not make borrowed owners static or every enclosing future Send.
safety_basis: Moving bookkeeping preserves uniquely owned static allocation and hardware endpoint addresses
Shared safe access does not dereference RX storage; every CPU RX copy uses an exclusive borrow
Interrupts retain synchronized state and owned Wakers, never driver, future or buffer pointers
Existing paired terminal, wire-idle and fenced retirement requirements remain before temporary CPU slices
Cancellation, unresolved Drop and forget retain allocations, channel admission, pins and required clock state

source_review.byte_preservation_qualification: Lifecycle order, checks and conditions remain preserved. DMA ownership representation, constructor initialization and private copy receiver/callers have the precise approved correction above; these bodies are not claimed byte-identical.
